gaps: G1: AttachmentOpenResult lacks the canonical fileName (computed at attachment-resolver.ts:326-329 but not returned) — the copy needs it.

G2: Telegram live attachments (and any provider without fetchHistoricalAttachment) have workspace-local storageRefs and no provider_fetch — unresolvable by the store path, so 'uniform across providers' was false as stated.
G3: the writer requires the destination directory to exist; the plan had not assigned the mkdir responsibility.
G4: long-running-list membership only prevents IPC head-of-line blocking; the runner-side timeout override is a separate mandatory change the plan conflated with it.
contradictions: C1: plan proposed returning raw bytes from a resolver mode — bytes are streamed and never buffered; the CAS materializedPath already reaches the handler, so the mode only needs to skip view extraction and add fileName.
C2: a bare fs.copyFile was implied viable — it would bypass the hardened destination guarantees; stream a reader into writeInboundAttachment instead.
resolutions: G1: extend AttachmentOpenResult with fileName in the materialize mode.

G2: workspace-local storageRefs return status already_in_workspace with the existing relative path (no copy); Slack live resolves via its provider_fetch re-fetch; fetcherless history stays honestly unreachable.
G3: handler mkdirs quarantine/ (0700) before the write, per provider-attachment-materialization.ts:100-102.
G4: add the type to ipc-long-running-task.ts AND give the tool its own 120s timeout constant (resolver self-abort 110s inherited).
C1: mode branches inside openWithinDeadline (inheriting tombstone checks), skips extraction, returns materializedPath + fileName.
C2: destination write goes through writeInboundAttachment with a reader (streamed, hardened).
